transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (AuroraCloud Partnerships), Elena Koslov (AuroraCloud Solutions), Mark Tan (AuroraCloud Marketplace PM)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on reference architecture for a joint marketplace listing and joint-solution packaging. Focus areas: VPC peering / Private deployment patterns, marketplace artifact requirements (images/Helm/Terraform), benchmark plan, security artifacts (SOC2/KMS), and operational observability (Redwood Console integration).

Topics:
- Marketplace packaging and listing workflow
- Reference architecture for AuroraCloud's managed VPC and peering into Redwood Private control plane
- Joint solution: deployment templates, billing/usage telemetry hooks
- Security & compliance: KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
- Benchmarks and performance validation plan

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay, uh, hey everyone thanks for making time today, we can start and we'll, we'll go through the plan for the reference arch and marketplace listing, um Luis do you want to kick off with the rough topology?
[00:22] Luis Ortega: Yeah sure, thanks Maya. So the main idea is AuroraCloud customers should be able to provision a Redwood Private instance or connect to Redwood Dedicated pools via VPC peering or privatelink style endpoints, so from a diagram perspective we have the customer VPC -> peer -> Redwood Private subnet, and uh there are two options, either we host a control plane in Aurora region or use our control plane with customer-managed VPC peering.
[00:45] Elena Koslov: Sorry Luis, quick clarification, when you say control plane in Aurora region do you mean the Redwood control plane replicated into Aurora's account or like a regional control plane managed by Redwood?
[00:54] Luis Ortega: Good question, yeah we mean a customer-managed control plane option where a lightweight controlplane VM or k8s controller runs in the customer's account, it calls back to Redwood for billing and model catalog, or alternatively the fully-hosted Redwood control plane can sit in our region and the customer's VPC just peers for data path. The latter is easier but some customers prefer the customer-run control plane for compliance.
[01:20] Samir Rao: Right and from Aurora's marketplace side we also have packaging constraints, like artifacts need to be container images plus a Helm chart or Terraform module for the provisioning. We also want a clear AMI-based option for customers who prefer that.
[01:35] Priya Patel: That matches our experience. For reference arch we typically provide: Helm chart, example values.yaml, an optional AMI for on-prem-ish installs, and Terraform snippets for VPC peering and route tables. We'll include KV cache tuning and quantization profile recommendations in the repo.
[01:52] Mark Tan: On the listing metadata, we need to show expected latency/throughput and supported model list — can you provide performance profiles for Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private variants?
[02:05] Maya Chen: Yes, we have perf profiles but they vary with sequence length and batch config. We'll provide a short table: model variant, typical p95 latency at 1 and 10 concurrent streams, tokens/sec throughput, and recommended batch sizes. Note that the numbers are approximate, and we should include a note about fallback variants and quantized builds.
[02:30] Elena Koslov: Also compliance: we require SOC 2 type II evidence and a KMS integration pattern; customers often ask if keys can be customer-managed.
[02:40] Luis Ortega: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations in our Private deployment. There is a small caveat: in the customer-managed control plane mode, keys live in the customer's account; when using Redwood-hosted control plane with VPC peering we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS via cross-account grants. I might have mumbled that a bit earlier, hope that made sense.
[03:05] Samir Rao: That's good. On marketplace listing we also need a short deployment time estimate and rollback/fallback behavior documented. Can you outline the rollout story e.g., canary or staged rollout?
[03:18] Priya Patel: Yeah, we support canary rollouts at the routing layer — you can tag versions and do a percentage-based split, plus automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model if the primary variant crosses an error or latency threshold. We'll include an example canary deployment manifest in the repo.
[03:36] Mark Tan: For the joint solution badge on Aurora marketplace we need a reference architecture diagram and a tech contact for support. Who should we point to for first-line triage?
[03:44] Maya Chen: For triage the AE is first line and Luis will be the SE contact, with Priya handling integration check-ins. I'll be the overall partnership owner for the listing.
[03:55] Samir Rao: Cool. On telemetry — we need to show what signals we can ingest into Aurora's monitoring and billing systems. Will Redwood expose per-route token counts and latency metrics?
[04:08] Luis Ortega: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns and latency histograms via our metrics API. We can ship a plugin example that posts a subset of metrics to Aurora's ingestion endpoint (we'll provide sample queries and a kinesis/S3 sink example).
[04:28] Elena Koslov: About packaging, any restrictions on base images? Some customers are sensitive to distro CVE counts.
[04:35] Priya Patel: We use slim distros and can provide a minimal build. We'll publish SBOMs with the images and can include a distroless variant if required.
[04:48] Mark Tan: One thing we saw with other partners (Novamarket) is confusion around autoscaling — if the marketplace deploys a Reserved Dedicated pool, how does autoscale behave?
[04:59] Maya Chen: For Dedicated reserved capacity pools autoscaling is policy-driven: you can configure minimum and maximum GPU nodes and burst capacity. Marketplace listings can include recommended autoscale policies for typical workload profiles. We'll surface that in the doc.
[05:15] Samir Rao: Great. Benchmarks: we'd like to run a joint benchmark on Aurora staging. Goal: validate 100k tokens/day steady workload and a p95 latency under 400ms for the baseline model at 512 context. Can Redwood run that in your Dedicated pool or should we spin up a Private demo instance?
[05:32] Luis Ortega: We can run in Redwood Dedicated on Aurora's staging region using a sandbox account, that will be fastest. If the customer needs keys in their account we can run the Private deployment in their account as well but that takes longer. For the benchmark we'll provide a small harness and sample prompts.
[05:48] Elena Koslov: Perfect. On legal/compliance, marketplace requires a data processing addendum and standard indemnities — I'll follow up with our legal team but can you share Redwood's standard DPA and SOC 2 report?
[05:59] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send the DPA and SOC 2 summary. Also we have an audit log export API that meets marketplace requirements for traceability.
[06:12] Mark Tan: Two small asks: can we include a quickstart that uses Aurora's managed DB for storing prompts and a sample Terraform module that wires up IAM roles?
[06:21] Priya Patel: Yep, we'll add a quickstart repo that shows using Aurora DB plus sample IAM and KMS grants.
[06:30] Samir Rao: Ok next steps and owners?
[06:33] Maya Chen: Quick recap: Redwood to share reference arch diagram, Helm chart + example values, perf profiles, SOC2 + DPA docs, and benchmark harness. Aurora to provide marketplace packaging checklist, security checklist, and staging account for benchmarks. We'll attach owners to the action items.
[06:48] Luis Ortega: One more note: some of our customers care about KV cache warmup and mem requirements — we'll document recommended KV cache sizes per model family and a warmup script. There might be a typo in my earlier note where I said KV "cash" in the doc, so watch spelling.
[07:05] Elena Koslov: Haha noted, typos cost us dearly in the portal.
[07:10] Mark Tan: Anything else?
[07:12] Maya Chen: Nothing major. We'll move to action items. Thanks everyone.

[07:20] End of recording (approx).

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution may be off; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "KV cache" -> "kay vee cash") but content captured for action items and next steps.
